# Topics

This folder groups the core thematic areas used to evaluate and manage ADHD care within the Danish healthcare system. It covers clinical performance metrics, demographic and educational outcomes, and the systemic challenges of data quality and regional variation. Additionally, it documents the governance structures, policy frameworks, and standardized clinical processes that guide assessment and treatment pathways across public and private providers.

## Pages

- [[topics/data-quality/index|Data Quality]] — Addresses systemic flaws in the ADHD-DATABASEN, such as incomplete data collection from private hospitals and unrecorded clinical treatments.
- [[topics/demographic/index|Demographic]] — Tracks population sizes, gender distributions, age groups, and regional variations for pediatric and adult ADHD assessment and treatment.
- [[topics/educational-outcome/index|Educational Outcome]] — Documents academic disparities, specifically the gap in primary school leaving exam pass rates between youths with ADHD and the general population.
- [[topics/governance/index|Governance]] — Details the steering committee's oversight of quality initiatives, including indicator prioritization driven by workforce shortages and legislative shifts.
- [[topics/indicators/index|Indicators]] — Groups specific measurable metrics like Indikator 7a+7b used to evaluate ADHD care quality and regional feedback on their application.
- [[topics/low-performance/index|Low Performance]] — Documents departments that fell below specific operational or clinical benchmarks in ADHD reporting.
- [[topics/non-compliance/index|Non Compliance]] — Highlights systemic failures to meet clinical standards, such as zero compliance for Indikator 3 and missing psychoeducation records in private hospitals.
- [[topics/outlier-performance/index|Outlier Performance]] — Identifies exceptionally high-performing psychiatric departments that met or exceeded an 80% performance threshold in clinical data.
- [[topics/performance/index|Performance]] — Tracks the systematic evaluation of clinical quality, timeliness, and adherence to national standards across Denmark's 11 specific indicators.
- [[topics/performance-change/index|Performance Change]] — Monitors year-over-year shifts in regional ADHD care outcomes, highlighting significant metric improvements in specific regions.
- [[topics/policy/index|Policy]] — Contains the formal frameworks, political strategies like the 10-Year Plan, and clinical guidelines governing ADHD treatment quality.
- [[topics/policy-change/index|Policy Change]] — Documents structural revisions to clinical indicators, such as splitting metrics to refine diagnostic criteria and improve cross-sectoral coordination.
- [[topics/policy-development/index|Policy Development]] — Tracks the formulation of clinical policies, including anticipated updates driven by forthcoming non-pharmacological treatment guidelines.
- [[topics/processes/index|Processes]] — Covers standardized clinical workflows like the ADHD treatment package, diagnostic assessment processes, and cross-sectoral coordination meetings.
- [[topics/quality-indicator/index|Quality Indicator]] — Details specific metrics used to track diagnostic timeliness and treatment modalities, including timeframes for diagnostic interviews.
- [[topics/quality-indicators/index|Quality Indicators]] — Groups the complete set of national clinical quality indicators for ADHD care, detailing process and result metrics across patient populations.
- [[topics/quality-standard/index|Quality Standard]] — Outlines the 90% compliance targets and regulatory benchmarks established for ADHD diagnostic and treatment indicators.
- [[topics/regional-variation/index|Regional Variation]] — Details geographic disparities in clinical indicators, educational achievements, and patient pathway volumes across Denmark's five healthcare regions.
